angle: Verified families. Protected privacy. Your nikah begins with trust.

research.insight: June 2026 is peak summer wedding season; Islamic auspicious dates in June–July drive the highest-intent search traffic among Muslim matrimony seekers globally.
Nearly 8 in 10 Muslims globally now use online matchmaking platforms, yet trust remains the #1 barrier to conversion — verified profiles and photo privacy are table-stakes conversion signals.
Photo privacy is Muslim women's top safety concern: blur-by-default controls, watermarks, and photo misuse prevention are proven conversion-critical trust signals.

NikahForever (founded 2019, 196 employees as of April 2026) differentiates via picture blurring and manual profile verification; Shaadi.com positions itself as 'India's Most Trusted' — trust is the category battleground.

Wali/guardian involvement is a genuine product need for diaspora Muslims in UK, USA, and Canada: platforms enabling family registration and wali participation see significantly higher trust scores and completion rates.
NRI matrimony is growing in 2026 with families spanning multiple countries; cross-border introductions require extra verification steps and strong privacy controls to convert.

Muslim Matrimony

There is someone written for you.

At Date Khaas, we built a space where that journey starts with dignity. Every family you meet has been verified before any introduction is made. Your photos are yours — shared only when you choose, only with families you already trust. And your wali or parents are welcome at every single step.

Your Photos, Your Terms

The one written for you is waiting too. This summer, take the step that matters most — and take it in a place that treats your search with the care it deserves.

Begin Your Journey →

items.title: LinkedIn — Trust Is the Product in Muslim Matrimony
items.body:
In Muslim matrimony, trust isn’t a feature — it’s the entire product.

We’ve been building Date Khaas with a single conviction: the search for a life partner should never feel like a security risk.

For many Muslim women, sharing a photo is an act of vulnerability. For families, the question is always: “But are they who they say they are?”

The platforms that win this space won’t be the ones with the most profiles. They’ll be the ones that can answer yes to three questions:

→ Is every profile verified before it reaches me?
→ Can I control exactly who sees my photo?
→ Can my wali or family be part of this from day one?

At Date Khaas, those aren’t aspirations. They’re how we built the product from the ground up — because when someone trusts you with the search for their life partner, that trust deserves to be earned completely, not assumed.

With nearly 8 in 10 Muslims now using online matchmaking platforms (NikahPlus, 2026), the category is established. The differentiation battle is being fought entirely on trust and safety.

The nikah journey begins long before the ceremony. It begins with a first introduction — and that introduction should feel safe.
